title: Bibliographical route from holomorphic to meromorphic residues
notes: Fedosov lists Michigan Math. J. 14 (1967), 231--244; J. Differential Geom. 1 (1967), 311--330; a 1970 Matematika translation; and Baum--Bott, pp.~29--47 in the de Rham volume.
statement: The first two entries are Bott\textquoteright s vector-field characteristic-number and holomorphic-residue papers. The fourth is Baum--Bott\textquoteright s meromorphic-vector-field extension. These are sources for, rather than new assertions beyond, the adjacent formulas.

title: Polar divisor of a meromorphic vector field
notes: The pole set is written as irreducible hypersurfaces \(Y_i\), with an effective cycle \(\sum\alpha_iY_i\). A local equation removes the pole of \(V\).
statement: For a meromorphic section \(V\) of \(TX\) on a complex manifold, choose an effective Cartier divisor \(D=\sum m_iY_i\) clearing its poles. Then \(V\) is a holomorphic section of \(TX\otimes\mathcal O(D)\), or equivalently a morphism \(\mathcal O(-D)\to TX\). Set \(\rho=c_1(\mathcal O(D))\in H^2(X;\mathbb Z)\).
reconstruction: The divisor is a real codimension-two cycle; the notes\textquoteright wording \emph{two-dimensional cycles} confuses degree and dimension. Local multiplicities and the line-bundle formulation are made explicit.
fate: This is the setup of the 1970 meromorphic residue theorem \citep[pp.~29--47]{baumbott1970zeroes}; its abstract explicitly uses a tangent field twisted by a line bundle. The exact virtual-bundle formulation is independently verified in \citet[\S4.5, Proposition 4.6]{bruzzorubtsov2012localization}; its notation \(L=\mathcal O(D)\) gives \(TX-L^*\).
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Regularized Chern classes of the meromorphic field
notes: \(a_1=c_1+\rho\), \(a_2=c_2+c_1\rho+\rho^2\), and \(a_i=c_i+c_{i-1}\rho+\cdots+\rho^i\).
statement: These are the degree-\(2i\) components of \(c(TX-\mathcal O(-D))=c(TX)/(1-\rho)\). They are classes of a virtual bundle of rank \(n-1\), not the ordinary Chern classes of \(TX\otimes\mathcal O(D)\).
reconstruction: The virtual-bundle identification is editorial; it prevents replacing the notebook\textquoteright s actual formula with a different tensor-product formula.
fate: Baum--Bott\textquoteright s meromorphic formulation is the prior source named in the notes \citep[pp.~29--47]{baumbott1970zeroes}. The algebraic identity is checked directly from the displayed notebook coefficients. The exact virtual-bundle formulation is independently verified in \citet[\S4.5, Proposition 4.6]{bruzzorubtsov2012localization}; its notation \(L=\mathcal O(D)\) gives \(TX-L^*\).
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Residues for meromorphic one-dimensional foliations
notes: The notes ask that the preceding holomorphic residue formula be applied using the regularized \(a_i\).
statement: Let \(X\) be compact complex of dimension \(n\), and \(L=\mathcal O(-D)\to TX\) a holomorphic line-bundle morphism with isolated nondegenerate zeros. For an invariant polynomial \(\phi\) of degree \(n\), its characteristic number on \(TX-L\) is the sum of local residues. In a local frame, with derivative matrix \(A_p\), the nondegenerate residue is \(\phi(A_p)/\det A_p\). Rescaling the local frame cancels because both numerator and denominator have degree \(n\).
reconstruction: Compactness, isolated zeros of the extended morphism, and nondegeneracy are supplied. Zeros created on the polar divisor must also be included; counting only zeros away from poles need not give the characteristic number.
fate: The prior source named in the notes is \citet[pp.~29--47]{baumbott1970zeroes}. The exact virtual-bundle formula and isolated-zero hypothesis were read in \citet[\S4.5, Proposition 4.6]{bruzzorubtsov2012localization}, which explicitly identifies it as the Baum--Bott theorem. The original 1970 proof was not retrieved.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Killing field and skew linearization
notes: The metric identity is \(([X,Y],Z)+(Y,[X,Z])=X(Y,Z)\); at a zero, the derivative \(\Theta_p\) is skew.
statement: A smooth vector field \(X\) is Killing when \(\mathcal L_Xg=0\). At a zero \(p\), \(A_p=(\nabla X)_p\) is skew-adjoint on \(T_pM\), and a nondegenerate zero means \(\det A_p\ne0\).
reconstruction: The displayed identity is read as a formula for the Riemannian inner product, not a Lie-algebra bilinear form.
fate: This is the infinitesimal-isometry framework used by \citet[pp.~173--193]{baumcheeger1969isometries}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Real localization formula with a signed Pfaffian
notes: For an oriented manifold of dimension \(4k\), the Pontryagin characteristic number is a sum of \(\psi(\Theta_p)/\operatorname{Pf}(\Theta_p)\).
statement: For a closed oriented Riemannian \(4k\)-manifold and a Killing field with isolated nondegenerate zeros, an invariant polynomial representing a Pontryagin number localizes as \(\int_M\psi(R/(2\pi))=\sum_p\psi(A_p)/\operatorname{Pf}(A_p)\), with matching Chern--Weil conventions. The Pfaffian uses the given orientation; it is not an unsigned square root of the determinant.
reconstruction: Closedness and isolated nondegenerate zeros are essential. A consistent normalization is specified; numerator and denominator have the same total degree, so common \(2\pi\) factors cancel.
fate: The prior infinitesimal-isometry result is \citet[pp.~173--193]{baumcheeger1969isometries}; Bott\textquoteright s 1967 characteristic-number work is also explicitly on the reading list \citep{bott1967vector}. Original result-level access was incomplete.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Equivalence and induced matrix deformations
notes: A matrix \(A(\lambda)\) depending on parameters is considered after changes of parameters and parameter-dependent similarity transformations.
statement: A deformation of \(A_0\in\operatorname{Mat}_n(\mathbb C)\) is a smooth or holomorphic germ \(A:(\mathbb C^r,0)\to(\operatorname{Mat}_n,A_0)\). Another deformation is induced if \(B(\mu)=S(\mu)^{-1}A(\varphi(\mu))S(\mu)\), where \(\varphi(0)=0\) and \(S(0)\) centralizes \(A_0\) (one may require \(S(0)=I\)). Versality means every deformation is so induced in the chosen category.
reconstruction: The smooth and holomorphic categories are separated; the notes do not authorize a topological classification under arbitrary homeomorphisms.
fate: Arnold\textquoteright s 1971 paper gives the parameter-dependent normal-form theory \citep[pp.~29--43]{arnold1971matrices}. The lecture precedes the journal issue; no earlier preprint date was established.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Transverse slices as versal parameter families
notes: Jordan normal forms organize the possible matrices, but smooth parameter-dependent normal forms require extra entries near repeated eigenvalues.
statement: At \(A_0\), the conjugacy orbit has tangent space \([A_0,\operatorname{Mat}_n]\). If \(V\) is a linear complement, then \(A_0+V\) is miniversal locally: the map \((S,v)\mapsto S^{-1}(A_0+v)S\) is a submersion at \((I,0)\). Its parameter dimension is \(\dim\ker\operatorname{ad}_{A_0}\).
reconstruction: The complement and submersion argument are a modern precise reconstruction. Jordan canonical form chosen independently at each parameter does not itself prove smooth versality.
fate: The normal-form framework matches \citet[pp.~29--43]{arnold1971matrices}; the detailed continuation and parameter count occur in record 218.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Gelfand’s proposed local model for general group actions
notes: Gelfand discusses high-order tensors and proposes that locally one has a nonsingular fibration plus a remaining adjoint/Jordan-form problem.
statement: The group, action, locality, topology, allowable equivalence, and meaning of the remaining adjoint problem are not fixed. This is a research heuristic, not a quantified slice theorem.
reconstruction: No universal theorem is supplied: a modern slice result for a specified proper or reductive action would add substantial assumptions not present here.
fate: Searches under Arnold\textquoteright s matrix paper and the Gelfand--Kazhdan bibliography give related normal-form/cohomology topics, not an exact publication of this general conjecture \citep{arnold1971matrices,gelfandkazhdan1971geometry}.

title: Weighted homogeneity and the isolated singularity
notes: For the weights \(w_i\), monomials satisfy \(\sum i_j/w_j=1\); \(f=0\) has an isolated critical point at the origin.
statement: Let \(f\in\mathbb C[z_1,\ldots,z_m]\) be weighted homogeneous of weighted degree one with positive rational coordinate weights \(q_i=1/w_i\), and suppose \(\nabla f\) vanishes only at \(0\). The Milnor fibre has reduced homology concentrated in degree \(m-1\); its rank is the Milnor number \(\mu\).
reconstruction: The notebook\textquoteright s \(w_i\) are reciprocals of a widespread modern weight convention. Reduced homology is required also for \(m=1\).
fate: This is the setting of \citet[pp.~385--393]{milnororlik1970weighted}; the modern formulation is checked in \citet[definition preceding Theorem~1.5]{hertlingmase2022weights}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Milnor number of a weighted homogeneous hypersurface
notes: \(\mu=\prod_i(w_i-1)\); the diagonal example is \(z_1^{a_1}+\cdots+z_m^{a_m}\).
statement: Under the isolated-critical-point hypothesis, \(\mu=\dim_{\mathbb C}\mathbb C[z]/(\partial f)=\prod_i(q_i^{-1}-1)\). For the Brieskorn polynomial with integers \(a_i\ge2\), this is \(\prod_i(a_i-1)\).
reconstruction: The finite-dimensional Jacobian algebra is supplied as the precise meaning of multiplicity; arbitrary positive rational weights without an isolated singularity do not suffice.
fate: The formula was published before the talk in \citet{milnororlik1970weighted}; its Jacobian-algebra interpretation is checked against \citet[Theorem~6.4(b)]{hertlingmase2022weights}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: The group-ring divisor calculation for monodromy
notes: In \(\mathbb Q[\mathbb C^*]\), \(E_k=k^{-1}\sum_{\zeta^k=1}[\zeta]\) is an idempotent. For reduced \(w_i=u_i/v_i\), the monodromy divisor is \(\prod_i(w_iE_{u_i}-1)\).
statement: Write \(\Lambda_d=\sum_{\zeta^d=1}[\zeta]\), with multiplication induced by multiplication of complex numbers. Then \(\Lambda_a\Lambda_b=\gcd(a,b)\Lambda_{\operatorname{lcm}(a,b)}\), and \(\operatorname{div}\det(tI-h_*)=\prod_i(\Lambda_{u_i}/v_i-[1])\). For an isolated weighted homogeneous singularity the final coefficients are nonnegative integers.
reconstruction: The symbol \(1\) denotes the identity group-ring element \([1]\). Rational intermediate coefficients do not mean the characteristic polynomial has fractional multiplicities.
fate: The monodromy formula is exactly the Milnor--Orlik theorem, explicitly restated in \citet[Theorem~6.4(a)]{hertlingmase2022weights}; the original paper is \citet{milnororlik1970weighted}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Polynomial-power distributions and cycles
notes: Bernstein connects poles or residues of \(P^\lambda\) with cycles and their transformations.
statement: The note does not specify the polynomial, real or complex distribution, integration cycle, pole, or claimed relation. Meromorphic continuation and monodromy are distinguishable questions; neither a precise residue formula nor a monodromy eigenvalue theorem is recorded.
reconstruction: No theorem is reconstructed from the general association.
