title: The Ray–Singer preprint and analytic torsion
notes: The notebook mentions a preprint by Singer \emph{and someone else} on an analytic expression for torsion.
statement: For a closed Riemannian manifold \(M\) and a unitary flat bundle \(E\), the positive Hodge-Laplacian spectrum defines \(\zeta_q(s)\). Analytic torsion is \(T(M,E)=\exp\{\frac12\sum_q(-1)^q q\zeta_q^{\prime}(0)\}\), with a stated torsion convention. For nonacyclic \(E\), comparison uses the corresponding determinant-line metric or compatible cohomology bases.
reconstruction: Daniel B. Ray is the missing coauthor. Zeta regularization is not an ordinary convergent product of all eigenvalues; zero modes are omitted.
fate: The preprint was circulating by this 1 March 1971 report; the paper appeared later in 1971 as \citet{raysinger1971torsion}. This identifies the construction, not a proof then available of the general equality. The original Introduction, p.~145, explicitly says the equality was not proved there; Definition 1.6 on p.~149 gives the zeta-regularized torsion.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Equality of analytic and Reidemeister torsion
notes: The preprint is described as expressing combinatorial torsion analytically; the status of a general equality is not separated from the proposal.
statement: For a closed smooth manifold and an acyclic unitary flat bundle, does Ray--Singer analytic torsion equal the corresponding positive Reidemeister torsion? With cohomology present the comparison is one of metrics on the determinant line.
reconstruction: The equality is identified as the Ray--Singer conjecture; it must not be reported as a theorem already proved by the 1971 preprint.
fate: Cheeger announced a proof in 1977 \citep[p.~2651, abstract]{cheeger1977torsion}; M\"uller\textquoteright s independent full paper appeared in 1978 \citep{muller1978torsion}. The original Ray--Singer Introduction, p.~145, independently confirms its conjectural status in 1971 \citep{raysinger1971torsion}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the unitary comparison is the established Cheeger--M"uller theorem. The notes do not formulate later nonunitary anomaly questions.

title: Schur determinant factorization
notes: For a block matrix, \(\det\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\C&D\end{pmatrix}=\det D\det(A-BD^{-1}C)\).
statement: For square \(A,D\) over \(\mathbb C\), conformable off-diagonal blocks, and invertible \(D\), the stated determinant identity follows from block Gaussian elimination.
reconstruction: Finite dimensions and invertibility are made explicit; no infinite-dimensional regularized determinant is meant. The same elementary identity already appears as 1964-17.2.
fate: This is the classical Schur-complement identity; the prior occurrence 1964-17.2 is reused as provenance. A modern reference is \citet[Chapter~1]{zhang2005schur}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Positivity through the Schur complement
notes: The notebook uses \(D\ge0\) and \(A-BD^{-1}C\ge0\) while concluding positive definiteness.
statement: If \(M=\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\B^*&D\end{pmatrix}\) is Hermitian and \(D>0\), then \(M>0\) iff \(A-BD^{-1}B^*>0\), and \(M\ge0\) iff the latter Schur complement is \(\ge0\). If \(D\) is singular, the inverse formula must be replaced by a pseudoinverse together with \(\operatorname{ran}B^*\subseteq\operatorname{ran}D\).
reconstruction: Hermitian symmetry, strict versus weak positivity, and invertibility are supplied. These are corrections of the mathematical shorthand, not new assumptions silently attributed to the speaker.
fate: The standard criterion is summarized in \citet[Chapter~1]{zhang2005schur}; the strict/weak distinction follows directly from the block congruence.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Determinant of an exact based complex
notes: Novikov assigns a determinant to \(0\to E_0\to\cdots\to E_n\to0\) by choosing bases in images and lifting them to neighboring terms.
statement: For a finite acyclic complex of finite-dimensional vector spaces over a field, fixed bases \(c_i\), boundary bases \(b_i\), and lifts of \(b_{i-1}\), torsion is the alternating product of the transition determinants \([b_i\widetilde b_{i-1}/c_i]^{(-1)^{i+1}}\), up to the explicitly chosen reciprocal/sign convention.
reconstruction: The bases in the complex itself are part of the data. Independence concerns auxiliary boundary bases and lifts, not arbitrary changes of all \(c_i\).
fate: The algebraic construction and its change-of-basis rules precede the lecture; see \citet[\S3]{milnor1966torsion}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Cancellation of auxiliary determinants
notes: The alternating product is said not to depend on the arbitrary intermediate choices.
statement: Changing a boundary basis contributes equal determinants in adjacent degrees with opposite exponents; changing its lift gives a block-unitriangular change. Therefore torsion is independent of these choices. Changing \(c_i\) multiplies it by the corresponding alternating determinant.
reconstruction: The elementary cancellation argument is expanded to specify precisely which basis-independence is true.
fate: This is the standard based-complex torsion invariance \citep[\S3]{milnor1966torsion}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Twisted cellular complex of a lens space
notes: The lens-space complex has differentials \(1-\xi\), \(1+\xi+\cdots+\xi^{p-1}\), and \(1-\xi^\beta\).
statement: For \(L(p,q)\), with \(p>1\), \(\gcd(p,q)=1\), and a nontrivial complex character taking a generator to \(\xi\), the twisted cellular chain complex has one one-dimensional term in degrees zero through three. Up to units/signs and the chosen generator, its maps are \(\xi-1,0,\xi^\beta-1\), with \(q\beta\equiv1\pmod p\). Both nonzero maps are invertible, so the twisted complex is acyclic.
reconstruction: The character is nontrivial and \(\xi\) need not be primitive provided \(\xi^p=1\); coprimality ensures \(\xi^\beta\ne1\). The universal-cover complex before twisting is not acyclic.
fate: The classical lens-space example and the role of a character are treated in \citet[\S12]{milnor1966torsion}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Lens-space determinant and the torsion convention
notes: The written answer is \((1-\xi)(1-\xi^\beta)\).
statement: With Novikov\textquoteright s alternating determinant convention one may obtain this product; with the usual chain-torsion convention \(\tau(L(p,q),\xi)\) is its reciprocal, modulo the units caused by cell lifts and orientations. The invariant must be quoted with its convention.
reconstruction: The notebook is not declared wrong merely because another convention inverts torsion. Its product is distinguished from an unconditional equality of canonically normalized complex numbers.
fate: The reciprocal convention and unit ambiguity are explicit in the lens-space torsion calculation \citep[\S12]{milnor1966torsion}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Versality is not a categorical final object
notes: A deformation inducing all nearby deformations is described as a final object.
statement: Versality requires existence of inducing parameter maps and conjugacies, not their uniqueness. Miniversality additionally minimizes the tangent parameter dimension. Nontrivial stabilizers generally obstruct the claimed final-object universal property.
reconstruction: The distinction between a versal object and a universal object is an editorial correction. It continues item 1970-213.1.
fate: Arnold\textquoteright s matrix-deformation framework is the precise match \citep[pp.~29--43]{arnold1971matrices}; metadata and abstract were checked, not the complete proof.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Nine parameters for Jordan blocks of sizes three and two
notes: A five-by-five Jordan matrix with a common eigenvalue and blocks of lengths three and two is supplied with nine starred perturbation entries.
statement: For \(A_0=J_3(\lambda)\oplus J_2(\lambda)\), the centralizer dimension is \(3+2+2+2=9\). A complement to \([A_0,\operatorname{Mat}_5]\) therefore yields a nine-parameter miniversal deformation. A particular star pattern is valid only if its coordinate subspace is such a complement.
reconstruction: The exact count is verified algebraically; the drawn placement of stars is not promoted into a uniquely determined normal form.
fate: This is a concrete instance of \citet{arnold1971matrices}, illustrated by the notebook itself.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Centralizer codimension and the dimension of a miniversal base
notes: For Jordan blocks, the parameter count is \(n_1+3n_2+5n_3+\cdots\), summed over eigenvalues.
statement: If the Jordan-block sizes for eigenvalue \(\lambda\) are \(n_{\lambda,1}\ge n_{\lambda,2}\ge\cdots\), then \(\dim Z(A)=\sum_\lambda\sum_{i,j}\min(n_{\lambda,i},n_{\lambda,j})=\sum_\lambda\sum_i(2i-1)n_{\lambda,i}\). This is the codimension of the conjugacy orbit and the dimension of a miniversal base.
reconstruction: The ordering of block sizes and separate summation over distinct eigenvalues are supplied.
fate: The formula and transverse-family interpretation are the theory announced in \citet{arnold1971matrices}; the centralizer count itself is elementary Jordan-module algebra.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: KdV through an evolving Schrödinger operator
notes: The notes write \(u_t+2u_{xxx}+6uu_x=0\), then associate \(-\partial_x^2+u\) to the initial potential.
statement: For real Schwartz initial data, one standard normalization is \(u_t-6uu_x+u_{xxx}=0\) with \(L=-\partial_x^2+u\). Inverse scattering evolves the reflection coefficient by a cubic phase, keeps the negative eigenvalues fixed, and evolves their norming constants exponentially; inverse reconstruction gives the KdV solution.
reconstruction: The standard normalization is stated separately. The literal coefficients on P000341 do not agree with the Hamiltonian displayed on P000342; changing signs or rescaling must be done consistently.
fate: The inverse-scattering method predates the talk; \citet[Introduction, equations (1)--(5)]{zakharovfaddeev1971kdv} explicitly reviews the earlier Gardner--Greene--Kruskal--Miura method.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Reflection, transmission, and complete scattering data
notes: The scattering solution behaves as \(e^{ikx}+a(k)e^{-ikx}\) at the left and \(b(k)e^{ikx}\) at the right, with \(|a|^2+|b|^2=1\).
statement: For real \(u\) with \(\int(1+|x|)|u(x)|\,dx<\infty\), real \(k\ne0\) defines reflection \(r(k)\) and transmission \(t(k)\) coefficients with \(|r|^2+|t|^2=1\). To reconstruct a potential with bound states, reflection data must be supplemented by the negative eigenvalues and positive norming constants.
reconstruction: The notebook\textquoteright s \(a,b\) are reflected/transmitted amplitudes, whereas the later paper uses different letters. The discrete spectrum alone does not supply the norming constants.
fate: The full data and inverse problem are stated in \citet[Introduction and \S1]{zakharovfaddeev1971kdv}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Reflectionless potentials and solitons
notes: When the reflected wave vanishes, one obtains solitons; the discrete spectrum remains relevant.
statement: A real rapidly decaying reflectionless potential with finitely many simple negative eigenvalues and their norming constants produces a finite soliton solution under KdV evolution. With no bound states and zero reflection the potential is zero.
reconstruction: Reflectionless does not mean absence of scattering data: the eigenvalues and norming constants encode the solitons.
fate: The scattering evolution and discrete variables are reviewed in \citet[Introduction, equations (4)--(5)]{zakharovfaddeev1971kdv}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Conservation laws and the absence of shock formation
notes: The margin associates infinitely many first integrals with the observation that shock waves do not arise.
statement: For a smooth decaying KdV solution, integrations by parts give conserved local integrals, beginning with \(\int u\), \(\int u^2\), and, in the stated normalization, \(\int(u^3+\tfrac12u_x^2)\). Smooth real Schwartz data yield global smooth solutions in this integrable setting. The mere existence of many formal integrals is not by itself a proof of regularity.
reconstruction: The qualitative observation is separated from the invalid general implication that an unspecified collection of first integrals rules out singularities.
fate: The established KdV integrals are listed in \citet[equation (2) and \S3]{zakharovfaddeev1971kdv}; the marginal explanatory claim is stronger than what that list alone proves.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Gardner’s Poisson bracket and a symplectic leaf
notes: A double-integral skew form on variations \(\delta u\) is written, and the Hamiltonian is displayed as \(Q=\int(u^3+u_x^2)\,dx\).
statement: The Hamiltonian operator \(J=\partial_x\) defines \(\{F,G\}=\int(\delta F/\delta u)\partial_x(\delta G/\delta u)\,dx\). On real Schwartz variations of zero integral, its inverse is \(\partial_x^{-1}v(x)=\frac12\int\operatorname{sgn}(x-y)v(y)\,dy\), giving a weak symplectic form. With \(H=\int(u^3+\tfrac12u_x^2)\,dx\), one obtains \(u_t=6uu_x-u_{xxx}\).
reconstruction: The fixed-mass leaf, skew inverse, and coefficient \(1/2\) specify a consistent convention. The literal notebook Hamiltonian yields \(6uu_x-2u_{xxx}\), not its earlier displayed equation.
fate: The paper credits the bracket to Gardner and records the consistent Hamiltonian \citep[equations (6)--(7)]{zakharovfaddeev1971kdv}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Trace identities and scattering expressions for local integrals
notes: The local integrals are expressed by moments of \(\log(1-|a|^2)\); the displayed expression for \(Q\) contains a \(k^4\) integral.
statement: For real Schwartz potentials, the high-energy expansion of the transmission coefficient gives a hierarchy of trace identities: each appropriate local KdV integral is a fixed multiple of a moment of \(\log(1-|r(k)|^2)\) plus a finite sum of powers of the bound-state parameters. The constants depend on the KdV and scattering conventions.
reconstruction: The notebook\textquoteright s schematic integral is not a complete equality when eigenvalues occur. No unchecked numerical coefficient is inserted into that display.
fate: The precise hierarchy and discrete terms appear in \citet[\S3, equations (25)--(30)]{zakharovfaddeev1971kdv}, received 14 June 1971.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Canonical scattering coordinates
notes: The skew form is rewritten using \(k\,\delta\log(1-|a|^2)\) and \(\delta\arg a\), with additional terms when eigenvalues exist.
statement: In the published scattering convention \(r=b/a\), canonical variables include \(P(k)=-(k/\pi)\log(1-|r(k)|^2)\) and \(Q(k)=\arg b(k)\), together with bound-state action--angle pairs. On charts where the phases are defined, the symplectic form is the continuous canonical integral plus the discrete sum. Phase variables are singular at zeros of the corresponding coefficient.
reconstruction: The notebook reflection coefficient is not automatically the paper\textquoteright s \(b\); replacing \(\arg b\) by \(\arg r\) without the induced corrections is unjustified. The paper explicitly calls its calculations formal derivations rather than a complete analytic manifold construction.
fate: This is the central new result of \citet[\S2, equations (22)--(24)]{zakharovfaddeev1971kdv}; the paper\textquoteright s methodological qualification is on p.~282.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Three-dimensional scattering amplitude and the unitary operator
notes: The asymptotic wave is \(e^{i\mathbf k\cdot x}+r^{-1}e^{ikr}f(k;\alpha,\beta)+o(r^{-1})\); \(f\) has five variables, and the notes write \(S(k)=I+f\), calling it unitary.
statement: For a real sufficiently regular short-range potential in \(\mathbb R^3\), positive energy \(k^2\) and incident/outgoing directions \(\alpha,\beta\in S^2\) define the amplitude. The on-shell scattering operator on \(L^2(S^2)\), with its normalization factor and identity term, is unitary. The amplitude kernel alone is not a unitary operator.
reconstruction: The factor relating the amplitude integral operator to \(S(k)-I\) is convention dependent. The dimensional count is one energy variable and two variables for each direction.
fate: The amplitude/operator distinction is explicit in \citet[p.~70, equations (5)--(8)]{faddeev1966factorization}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Volterra factorization of the multidimensional scattering operator
notes: The notes factor \(S(k)\) by \(Q_\gamma^{\pm}\), with kernels supported on one side of \((\alpha-\beta)\cdot\gamma=0\), and mention analytic continuation of diagonal data.
statement: Faddeev\textquoteright s factorization uses modified Green functions and a fixed direction \(\gamma\). Provided the corresponding Fredholm equation is uniquely solvable, the resulting factors are triangular with respect to the angular order and recover \(S\); their diagonal data have the specified complex-direction continuation. The 1966 note assumes unique solvability and explicitly proves it only in a sufficiently small-potential regime.
reconstruction: The notebook signs and factor order depend on incoming/outgoing conventions. The uniqueness hypothesis is material; the construction is not an unconditional global inverse theorem for all decaying potentials.
fate: The precise prior source is \citet[pp.~71--72, equations (10)--(13)]{faddeev1966factorization}, received 3 June 1965 and published in 1966.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: The discrete-spectrum obstruction in the inverse problem
notes: The Green function and factorization had been written down earlier, but \ru{Обратной задачи не было из-за дискретного спектра}.
statement: This is a historical report about the method\textquoteright s unresolved analytic continuation and exceptional parameters. It does not specify a modern inverse-data problem, a uniqueness class, or a claimed obstruction for every potential.
reconstruction: It is not converted into a present-day open inverse-scattering conjecture.
fate: The earlier paper explicitly left singularities of the continued modified solutions uncontrolled \citep[p.~72]{faddeev1966factorization}; the notebook does not identify a stronger exact question.
present_status: As of November 2026, the historical limitation is identifiable, but no definite surviving open problem follows from this sentence.

title: Periods of rational differential forms
notes: \(\omega=P(z)Q(z)^{-1}dz_1\wedge\cdots\wedge dz_n\), \(V=\{Q=0\}\), and \(\int_\Gamma\omega\) for \(n\)-cycles in the complement.
statement: A closed rational top form on \(U=\mathbb C^n\setminus V\) pairs with \(H_n(U;\mathbb Z)\) by integration. After projective compactification all polar components, including a possible hyperplane at infinity, must be included in the divisor.
reconstruction: Closedness of a holomorphic top form is automatic on \(U\); a projective denominator must account for infinity rather than just the affine zero set.
fate: The bibliography identifies \citet[Part~I]{griffiths1969periods1} as the prior source; the exact subject is stated in the notebook itself.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: One-variable pole reduction and residues
notes: Homology is generated by small loops around poles; higher-order poles are removed by subtracting exact differentials.
statement: For a rational one-form on the punctured complex line, partial fractions split it into an exact rational differential plus a sum of simple-pole forms. Its period around a cycle is \(2\pi i\) times the integral linear combination of the enclosed residues.
reconstruction: The conventional \(2\pi i\) is restored; polynomial terms and all poles of order at least two contribute exact differentials.
fate: This elementary prototype is the starting point of the rational-period exposition \citep{griffiths1969periods1}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Middle-dimensional complement cycles vanish in projective space
notes: \(H_n(\mathbb P^n\setminus V;\mathbb Z)\to H_n(\mathbb P^n;\mathbb Z)\) is zero; the even-dimensional case uses Bézout.
statement: For a nonempty smooth hypersurface \(V\subset\mathbb P^n(\mathbb C)\) of degree \(q>0\), inclusion sends every middle-dimensional complement cycle to zero in projective homology. For odd \(n\), the target is zero. For \(n=2m\), intersecting with \(V\cap\mathbb P^{m+1}\), whose class is \(q[\mathbb P^m]\), forces its coefficient to vanish.
reconstruction: Positive degree and the torsion-free ambient group are explicit. The notebook\textquoteright s intersection proof is retained, rather than inferred from vanishing of a different cohomology group.
fate: The projective-complement framework belongs to \citet{griffiths1969periods1}; the complete elementary argument is present in the notes and repeated in record 222.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: The tube map and its surjectivity in middle dimension
notes: If \(\Gamma=\partial R\), take \(\gamma=R\cap V\); the circle tube \(\tau(\gamma)\) is homologous to \(\Gamma\).
statement: For smooth \(V\), the oriented real rank-two normal bundle gives a tube homomorphism \(\tau:H_k(V;\mathbb Z)\to H_{k+1}(\mathbb P^n\setminus V;\mathbb Z)\). In degree \(k=n-1\), it is surjective by the preceding vanishing and the long exact sequence of the pair plus the Thom isomorphism.
reconstruction: The tube is the normal circle bundle over the cycle, not an arbitrary full neighborhood of the cycle in projective space. Chain orientations fix a possible conventional boundary sign.
fate: This is the residue/tube construction underlying \citet{griffiths1969periods1}; record 222 supplies the exact sequence.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Harnack’s bound and real sextic configurations
notes: For degree \(n=2k\), the number of ovals is at most \(g+1\), \(g=(n-1)(n-2)/2\). A separate note says degree six has “50 cases (Gudkov)” and sketches an eleven-oval arrangement.
statement: A nonsingular real projective plane curve of even degree \(2k\) has at most \((2k-1)(k-1)+1\) connected components, all ovals. For degree six the maximum is eleven. The unqualified number fifty does not specify whether empty curves, isotopy schemes, or a partial classification are counted.
reconstruction: The numerical shorthand is not substituted for the number of all real schemes. The maximal-oval illustration is separated from that unresolved bibliographical count.
fate: Arnold recalls Harnack and Gudkov\textquoteright s maximal sextics in \citet[\S1]{arnold1971ovals}. The exact interpretation of the notebook\textquoteright s “50” was not established.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Petrovskii’s inequalities for even-degree plane curves
notes: Writing \(p,m\) for ovals inside an even or odd number of other ovals gives \(|2(p-m)-1|\le3k^2-3k+1\).
statement: For a nonsingular real projective plane curve of degree \(2k\), let \(p\) and \(m\) denote the numbers of even and odd ovals. Petrovskii\textquoteright s inequalities are equivalent to the displayed double inequality. Maximality is not needed for this bound.
reconstruction: “Positive oval” in the notes means even nesting parity, not orientation of the oval.
fate: The prior inequalities are recalled in \citet[\S1]{arnold1971ovals}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Gudkov’s congruence modulo eight
notes: \(p-m\equiv k^2\pmod8\), following the discussion of curves with the maximal number of ovals.
statement: For a nonsingular real projective \(M\)-curve of degree \(2k\), meaning it has \((2k-1)(k-1)+1\) components, one has \(p-m\equiv k^2\pmod8\). Without the \(M\)-curve hypothesis this is not the asserted theorem.
reconstruction: The maximality hypothesis is carried forward from the preceding paragraph and stated explicitly.
fate: Rokhlin proved the exact congruence \citep[\S1]{rokhlin1972gudkov}; his note was received 29 December 1971 and published in 1972.
present_status: As of November 2026, solved: this is the Gudkov--Rokhlin congruence, not an unresolved part of Hilbert	extquoteright s sixteenth problem.

title: Arnold–Varchenko’s modulo-four result
notes: Arnold and Varchenko have proved \(p-m\equiv k^2\pmod4\) using quadratic forms.
statement: For every nonsingular real projective \(M\)-curve of even degree \(2k\), the weaker congruence modulo four holds.
reconstruction: The published paper is authored by Arnold; its final discussion acknowledges Varchenko\textquoteright s initial argument and the development of the proof. Joint spoken attribution is not silently changed into joint publication authorship.
fate: \citet[\S1 and final acknowledgments]{arnold1971ovals}, received 22 March 1971, publishes the result after the 15 March lecture.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Characteristic squares are well defined modulo eight
notes: For a characteristic \(u\), \((u+2x)^2=u^2+4(u,x)+4x^2\), and the two latter terms have matching parity.
statement: For an integral symmetric bilinear form, if \((u,x)\equiv(x,x)\pmod2\) for every \(x\), then \((u+2x,u+2x)\equiv(u,u)\pmod8\). This calculation proves independence of the characteristic lift, not yet the equality with the signature.
reconstruction: The distinction between lift independence and the full van der Blij lemma prevents treating the displayed two-line calculation as a proof of both assertions.
fate: The arithmetic tool is used in \citet{arnold1971ovals} and developed explicitly in record 225.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Branched double covers connect real curves with intersection forms
notes: The notes introduce \(z^2=f(x,y)\) and identify \(p-m\) with an Euler characteristic of a region of the real plane.
statement: For a smooth real plane curve of even degree, the corresponding double cover of \(\mathbb P^2(\mathbb C)\), branched along its complexification, is a compact smooth complex surface. Real involutions and their fixed loci connect nesting data to its integral intersection form; characteristic-vector congruences then constrain the ovals.
reconstruction: The affine equation is compactified via the square root line bundle \(\mathcal O(k)\). Smoothness of the branch curve is required. The full topology is sourced, not claimed proved by the single notebook line.
fate: This method is developed in \citet[\S\S2--8]{arnold1971ovals}; Rokhlin\textquoteright s stronger proof explicitly builds on it \citep[\S2]{rokhlin1972gudkov}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: The integral tube exact sequence and the kernel question
notes: The question \(\ker\tau=?\) is answered by \(H_{n+1}(\mathbb P^n)\to H_{n-1}(V)\to H_n(\mathbb P^n\setminus V)\to H_n(\mathbb P^n)\), followed by \(\ker\tau=H_{n+1}(\mathbb P^n)\).
statement: For a smooth positive-degree hypersurface, the pair sequence and the oriented Thom isomorphism give an exact sequence over \(\mathbb Z\). Precisely, \(\ker\tau=\operatorname{im}(H_{n+1}(\mathbb P^n;\mathbb Z)\xrightarrow{\cap V}H_{n-1}(V;\mathbb Z))\). Thus the kernel is zero for even \(n\); for \(n=2m+1\), it is generated by the hyperplane-section class \([V\cap\mathbb P^{m+1}]\).
reconstruction: The image, not the domain as a literal subgroup equality, is the kernel. Exactness needs no passage modulo torsion. The ambient source is injective here because intersecting its image with a suitable power of the hyperplane class has nonzero degree.
fate: This continues the tube construction in \citet{griffiths1969periods1}; the proof is reconstructed directly from the exact sequence already written in the notes.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: A closed chain need not bound
notes: The proof says \(\partial(T\gamma-R)=0\), hence \(T\gamma-R\) is a boundary.
statement: The closed chain \(T\gamma-R\) defines an ambient homology class. Its intersection with \(V\) gives \(\gamma\), establishing membership in the image of the intersection map. There is no need, and in general no justification, to declare the ambient cycle a boundary.
reconstruction: This repairs the notebook\textquoteright s proof of exactness without changing the intended sequence.
fate: The corrected chain argument is the ordinary proof of the pair/Thom exact sequence used in the rational-period construction \citep{griffiths1969periods1}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Homogeneous rational forms on projective space
notes: \(\Omega=\sum(-1)^j\xi_j\,d\xi_0\wedge\cdots\widehat{d\xi_j}\cdots\wedge d\xi_n\), and \(P\Omega/Q^\ell\) descends to projective space.
statement: If \(Q\) is homogeneous of degree \(q\) and \(P\) of degree \(\ell q-(n+1)\), then \(P\Omega/Q^\ell\) is horizontal and invariant under \(\mathbb C^*\), hence descends to a rational \(n\)-form on \(\mathbb P^n\). The formula \(\deg P=q-(n+1)\) applies only to a simple pole.
reconstruction: The pole-order factor \(\ell\) is missing from the final repeated degree formula on P000349; the earlier simple-pole formula on P000348 is correct.
fate: This is the homogeneous form setup of \citet{griffiths1969periods1}; its degree is independently checked by scaling every coordinate.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Lower-degree basic forms by contraction with the Euler field
notes: A more general alternating expression omits several \(d\xi_j\), and gives \(\deg B=\deg A+n+2-\ell\).
statement: Let \(E=\sum\xi_i\partial_{\xi_i}\) and let \(\eta\) be a polynomial \((r+1)\)-form with homogeneous coefficients of degree \(a\). If \(B\) has degree \(a+r+1\), then \((\iota_E\eta)/B\) is a horizontal, scaling-invariant rational \(r\)-form. With \(r=n+1-\ell\), its degree condition is exactly the one in the notes.
reconstruction: The lengthy coordinate formula is interpreted as Euler contraction; this states a clean sufficient descent construction rather than an unchecked claim about every possible presentation.
fate: The basic-form construction is part of the projective rational-form calculus cited as \citet{griffiths1969periods1}; scaling and \(\iota_E^2=0\) check the asserted property.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Griffiths reduction of a Jacobian numerator
notes: Subtracting a coboundary yields \(P=\ell\sum A_jQ_j-Q\sum\partial_jA_j\).
statement: For homogeneous \(Q\) of degree \(q\), \(\ell\ge1\), and homogeneous \(A_j\) of degree \(\ell q-n\), one has \(\frac{(\sum A_j\partial_jQ)\Omega}{Q^{\ell+1}}\equiv\frac{1}{\ell}\frac{(\sum\partial_jA_j)\Omega}{Q^\ell}\pmod{d\Omega^{n-1}(\mathbb P^n\setminus V)}\). Thus a numerator in the Jacobian ideal can be reduced by one pole order. A general numerator need not be in that ideal.
reconstruction: The two numerator degrees are distinguished, and the reduction is a cohomological congruence. Smoothness of \(V\) supports the subsequent finite Jacobian-ring description, although the displayed differentiation identity itself is algebraic.
fate: This is the Griffiths pole-reduction mechanism, explicitly attributed in the notes to \citet{griffiths1969periods1}. Exact differentiation supplies the stated reconstruction; the original 1969 full text was not successfully retrieved.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Characteristics must use the differential module of the system
notes: \ru{Надо выписать все следствия и с ними иметь дело}: all differential consequences must be included.
statement: For an analytic linear differential system represented by a coherent module \(\mathcal M\) over the sheaf of differential operators, the characteristic support is the support of \(\operatorname{gr}\mathcal M\) for a good filtration. Taking only the symbols of an arbitrary initial generating list may omit principal symbols of differential consequences.
reconstruction: The coherent differential-module formulation is a modern reconstruction of the method, not terminology asserted to occur in the notes.
fate: Palamodov\textquoteright s earlier work on differential operators in coherent analytic sheaves is a thematic source \citep{palamodov1968coherent}; the notebook does not identify a particular theorem from it.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: The displayed two-equation example is inconsistent
notes: The system \(D_xu=f\), \((D_y+\lambda)u=g\) is followed by \(u=D_yg-D_xf\). The scan confirms the written \(\lambda\).
statement: For constant \(\lambda\) and commuting partial derivatives, the actual compatibility is \(D_xg-D_yf=\lambda f\); it does not recover \(u\). An instructive different example would use \((D_y+x)u=g\), when \([D_x,D_y+x]u=u\) gives \(u=D_xg-(D_y+x)f\).
reconstruction: The latter system is explicitly an editorial illustration, not a proposed transcription of \(\lambda\). Both the notebook coefficient and its consequent fail to yield the claimed relation.
fate: The general differential-consequence principle matches Palamodov\textquoteright s work \citep{palamodov1968coherent}; the intended specific example cannot be identified from the surviving formula.
present_status: As of November 2026, the literal countercalculation is decisive, but the author	extquoteright s intended example is not recoverable.

title: Underdetermined divergence separates existence from uniqueness
notes: For \(D_xu+D_yv=f\), Holmgren\textquoteright s theorem works in no direction, while Cauchy--Kovalevskaya works in every direction.
statement: For analytic \(f\) in two variables, in any chosen nonzero normal direction one can solve for a normal derivative of one component after prescribing the other analytic component, giving local analytic solutions with compatible data. The equation alone does not uniquely determine both \(u\) and \(v\) from data on a hypersurface; hence a scalar Holmgren uniqueness conclusion cannot simply be transferred to this underdetermined system.
reconstruction: The statement is an existence/uniqueness contrast, not a contradiction between the two theorems. The arbitrary free component must be included.
fate: The example illustrates the theory of systems underlying \citet{palamodov1968coherent}; no exact publication match for this pedagogical example was found.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Finite-dimensional orbit alternatives
notes: The limit behavior of \(x,Ax,A^2x,\ldots\) is described as zero, infinity, or a compact set excluding zero.
statement: For a linear map on a finite-dimensional real or complex normed space and a fixed vector, either \(A^nx\to0\), or \(\|A^nx\|\to\infty\), or the orbit is bounded and its omega-limit set is nonempty compact and avoids zero. This follows by separating generalized eigenspaces with spectral radius below, equal to, or above one, and the polynomial growth of nontrivial Jordan chains.
reconstruction: “Limit points” means asymptotic behavior; infinity is not an ordinary point of the vector space, and the full orbit closure also contains initial transient points.
fate: This contrast supplies the finite-dimensional background to Rolewicz\textquoteright s previously published example \citep{rolewicz1969orbits}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Rolewicz’s hypercyclic multiple of the backward shift
notes: \(S(x_1,x_2,\ldots)=(x_2,x_3,\ldots)\), \(A=aS\), \(a>1\), can have an everywhere dense orbit on \(\ell^p\) or \(c^0\).
statement: On \(\ell^p(\mathbb N)\), \(1\le p<\infty\), or \(c_0(\mathbb N)\), over \(\mathbb R\) or \(\mathbb C\), the bounded operator \(\lambda S\) is hypercyclic when \(|\lambda|>1\). The separability restriction excludes \(\ell^\infty\).
reconstruction: The index range and complex analogue \(|\lambda|>1\) are supplied. The Hilbert-space example is \(p=2\); no theorem about every Hilbert space dimension is intended.
fate: \citet[pp.~17--22]{rolewicz1969orbits} appeared in 1969; the author\textquoteright s own institutional account identifies it as his hypercyclic example.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Concatenating small blocks to obtain a dense orbit
notes: A list of finite rational blocks is concatenated after long zero gaps, with block \(j\) divided by a suitable power of \(a\).
statement: Choose a dense sequence of finite-support vectors \(v_j\) with each target repeated, and increasing positions \(N_j\). Put the block \(\lambda^{-N_j}v_j\) at position \(N_j\), choosing later positions so that the tail after applying \((\lambda S)^{N_j}\) has norm below \(2^{-j}\) and all scaled block norms are summable. Then \((\lambda S)^{N_j}x-v_j\to0\), proving density.
reconstruction: The long gaps must control amplified later tails as well as place blocks without overlap; this quantitative choice fills the notebook\textquoteright s proof sketch. For complex spaces use rational real and imaginary parts.
fate: The construction explains the prior result \citep{rolewicz1969orbits}; the detailed tail condition is an editorial unpacking of the notebook, not a new theorem.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Topological conjugacy preserves a dense orbit
notes: \(A=UBU^{-1}\) for a homeomorphism \(U\); orbit density is a topological property.
statement: If \(U:X\to Y\) is a homeomorphism with \(UA=BU\), then \(U(\{A^nx\})=\{B^nU(x)\}\). Therefore hypercyclicity is invariant under topological conjugacy, even when \(U\) is nonlinear.
reconstruction: No claim of linear similarity follows from topological equivalence.
fate: The invariant is an immediate consequence of the definition and contextualizes \citet{rolewicz1969orbits}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: An algebraic operator unbounded in every norm
notes: One can construct an operator unbounded in every norm.
statement: On the algebraic vector space of finite-support sequences, define \(Te_n=ne_n\). For every norm on this space, a bound \(\|Tx\|\le C\|x\|\) would imply \(n\le C\) for all \(n\), so no such bound exists.
reconstruction: The example is editorial and proves a natural literal existential reading. The notes give no ambient space, completeness requirement, or specific operator, so they do not identify this particular construction.
fate: The sentence was searched together with Rolewicz\textquoteright s algebraic-operator and orbit work; no exact publication or intended ambient space was established. The institutional bibliography records \emph{Equations in linear spaces} (1968), but that broad title is not an exact match.
present_status: As of November 2026, the existential algebraic reading is elementary and true; the intended generality is unidentified, not an open problem.

title: Unimodular lattices, parity, and characteristic elements
notes: \(\varphi:\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb Z^n\to\mathbb Z\) is unimodular when it identifies the lattice with its dual. Rank, signature, and types I/II are listed.
statement: An integral symmetric nondegenerate form is unimodular when its determinant is \(\pm1\). It is even if \((x,x)\) is even for every \(x\), and odd otherwise. Because reduction modulo two is nondegenerate, the linear functional \(x\mapsto(x,x)\bmod2\) has a unique representing class \(u\in L/2L\), called characteristic.
reconstruction: Symmetry and nondegeneracy are supplied. “Type I” denotes odd and “type II” even; the characteristic vector is unique only modulo \(2L\).
fate: The notebook\textquoteright s cited arithmetic text treats these forms in Chapter~V \citep{serre1970arithmetic}. Earlier lectures underlying the book date to 1962 and 1964.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Van der Blij’s characteristic-signature congruence
notes: \(\varphi(u,u)\bmod8\) is independent of the lift and equals \(\operatorname{sgn}\varphi\bmod8\); a Fresnel integral is mentioned.
statement: For an integral unimodular symmetric bilinear lattice and any characteristic vector \(u\), \((u,u)\equiv\sigma(L)\pmod8\). In particular, an even unimodular lattice has signature divisible by eight.
reconstruction: Unimodularity is needed for the signature assertion; the simpler lift-independence calculation is separately recorded in 1970-221.5. The mention of a Fresnel integral is a proof method, not a supplied analytic proof.
fate: The classical arithmetic result is used explicitly by \citet{arnold1971ovals} and belongs to the unimodular-form treatment cited as \citet[Chapter~V]{serre1970arithmetic}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Classification of indefinite integral unimodular forms
notes: Rank, signature, and parity are complete invariants in the indefinite case; odd forms diagonalize, and even forms use \(U\) and \(\Gamma_8\).
statement: An odd indefinite unimodular lattice of signature \((p,q)\), \(p,q>0\), is \(I_{p,q}\). An even indefinite unimodular lattice exists exactly when \(p-q\equiv0\pmod8\) and is unique for that signature; it is an orthogonal sum of hyperbolic planes and copies of signed \(E_8\).
reconstruction: The sign of \(E_8\) is chosen to realize either signature. The indefinite hypothesis is indispensable; rank and signature alone do not distinguish parity.
fate: The exposition points to \citet[Chapter~V]{serre1970arithmetic}; the publisher\textquoteright s description confirms this chapter\textquoteright s subject, but its full theorem text was not retrieved.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Finiteness in the positive-definite case
notes: Positive-definite unimodular forms are finite in number in every dimension.
statement: For each fixed rank \(n\), there are finitely many isometry classes of positive-definite integral unimodular lattices. This is finiteness of classes, not uniqueness or an explicit classification by rank and signature.
reconstruction: Equivalence means integral lattice isometry, and the determinant is fixed at one. Without fixing determinant the assertion would be false.
fate: This is the definite reduction-theory counterpart of the Chapter~V discussion in \citet{serre1970arithmetic}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: What kind of stabilization erases parity?
notes: The final line says that stably only rank and signature remain, followed by “Dear Misha you are wrong.”
statement: If stabilization means adding only hyperbolic even planes \(U\), parity remains invariant, so rank and signature do not suffice. If both forms may be augmented by the same odd indefinite plane \(\langle1\rangle\oplus\langle-1\rangle\), then forms of equal rank and signature become odd indefinite and hence isometric by the classification theorem.
reconstruction: The notes do not identify the permitted stabilizations or the target of the handwritten disagreement. The two precise readings are kept separate.
fate: The arithmetic classification in \citet[Chapter~V]{serre1970arithmetic} explains both readings, but does not identify which was intended here.
present_status: As of November 2026, the ambiguity is terminological and does not produce a new unsolved classification problem.

title: Fiber products and their universal property
notes: The object \(B\times_A C\) completes a commutative square and every compatible pair of maps to \(B,C\) factors through it uniquely.
statement: For maps \(B\to A\leftarrow C\), a fiber product represents pairs \((X\to B,X\to C)\) whose composites to \(A\) agree. Its structure maps and unique factorization are part of the definition.
reconstruction: Compatibility with the maps to \(A\) is explicit; an arbitrary pair of maps does not suffice. This reprises item 1967-143.1.
fate: This standard prerequisite is used in \citet[\S1]{geronimus1971topology} and the site axioms \citep[Tag 00VH]{stacks2026sites}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Covering families define a Grothendieck pretopology
notes: The conditions are composition of coverings, stability under base change, and \(U\to U\) being a cover; the last axiom number is overwritten.
statement: A pretopology specifies covering families, contains identity covers, is stable under pullback, and is closed under composing a cover with covers of its members. Required pullbacks must exist; these families generate a Grothendieck topology by covering sieves.
reconstruction: The family axioms describe a pretopology. The overwritten numeral is immaterial. Related definitions occur in 1967-143.2 and 1968-151.1.
fate: Geronimus uses this framework \citep[\S1]{geronimus1971topology}; precise modern family axioms are in \citet[Tag 00VH, Definition 7.6.2]{stacks2026sites}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: The sheaf axiom is an equalizer condition
notes: A contravariant functor \(F:C\to K\) is followed by \(0\to F(A)\to\prod F(U_\alpha)\rightrightarrows\prod F(U_\alpha\times_AU_\beta)\).
statement: For a set-valued presheaf, \(F(A)\) must be the equalizer of the restriction maps to overlaps for every cover. In an abelian target this is \(0\to F(A)\to\prod F(U_\alpha)\xrightarrow{d}\prod F(U_\alpha\times_AU_\beta)\), with \(d\) the difference of restrictions. General target categories need the stated limits.
reconstruction: Zero and exact-sequence notation cannot literally be imposed on an arbitrary category \(K\).
fate: The matching condition is recorded by \citet[Tag 00VM, Definition 7.7.1]{stacks2026sites} and used by \citet[\S1]{geronimus1971topology}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Čech cohomology and associated sheaves
notes: For a cover \(\mathcal U\), one forms \(H(\mathcal U,F)\); a marked nontrivial theorem says that the preceding construction produces a sheaf.
statement: For an abelian presheaf, overlap products give a Čech complex for each cover. The matching-family plus construction, applied twice, gives the associated sheaf. Čech cohomology of one cover need not equal derived sheaf cohomology without acyclicity hypotheses; a spectral sequence relates them.
reconstruction: The unspecified construction is matched cautiously with Geronimus\textquoteright s sheafification discussion. No claim that one cover computes all cohomology is inserted.
fate: \citet[Propositions 1.3 and 1.6]{geronimus1971topology} supplies the associated-sheaf construction and cohomological spectral sequence.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Geronimus’s site of smooth group actions
notes: Objects are \(G\)-manifolds and morphisms are called regular \(G\)-maps with surjective tangent maps.
statement: For a Lie group \(G\), take smooth \(G\)-manifolds with all smooth equivariant maps as morphisms. A family is a cover when its members are equivariant submersions whose images jointly cover the target. Covers are stable under base change and composition.
reconstruction: Submersion is a condition on covering arrows, not every morphism.
fate: The short announcement \citet[\S0]{geronimus1971lie}, received 28 August 1970 and published in the first 1971 issue, precedes this April exposition. The detailed construction is \citet[\S3.1]{geronimus1971topology}, received 22 September 1970 and published later in 1971.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Finite-group representations as sheaves on the group-set site
notes: For finite \(G\), take finite \(G\)-sets and vector spaces; a representation \(T\) gives tuples satisfying \(\xi_{g i}=T_g\xi_i\). All sheaves arise this way.
statement: On finite left \(G\)-sets with jointly surjective equivariant covers, sheaves of vector spaces over a fixed field are equivalent to linear representations of \(G\). A module \(E\) gives \(F_E(X)=\operatorname{Map}_G(X,E)\); evaluation at the regular \(G\)-set recovers \(E\) and its action.
reconstruction: The topology and coefficient field are supplied. The five-point illustration does not restrict the equivalence to five-element sets.
fate: Geronimus identifies this older finite/discrete-group construction and credits Artin in the introduction and \S2 \citep{geronimus1971topology}; \citet[Theorem 1]{geronimus1971lie} records its cohomological comparison.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: A Lie-group representation gives an equivariant-function sheaf
notes: From \(X,T_g\) construct vector-valued functions \(\xi\), with \(T_g\xi(xg^{-1})=\xi(x)\). There are sheaves not obtained from representations.
statement: For a continuous Banach representation \(E\) of a Lie group, smooth equivariant maps \(X\to E\) form a sheaf on the submersion site. Its value on \(G\) is the space \(E^\infty\) of smooth vectors. The finite-group equivalence does not justify an equivalence with all continuous Banach representations in the Lie-group case.
reconstruction: Left and right conventions are reconciled by equivariance. The wider non-equivalence claim depends on the category of representations, which the notes omit; it is not asserted for every generalized notion of representation.
fate: \citet[\S7.1 and Proposition 7.3]{geronimus1971topology} gives the function sheaf and recovers the Gårding space. The comparison is announced in \citet[Theorem 3]{geronimus1971lie}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Classifying-space and differentiable cohomology comparisons
notes: Sometimes the construction gives cohomology of a topological space, sometimes cohomology as in Gelfand--Fuchs.
statement: For the group-action site of a connected Lie group \(G\), the sheaf of locally constant functions with values in a fixed discrete abelian group \(A\), with trivial action on the coefficient group, gives \(H^*(BG;A)\). For the smooth equivariant-function sheaf of a continuous Banach representation, site cohomology agrees with the differentiable group cohomology denoted \(H_{\rm alg}^*(G;E^\infty)\) by Geronimus.
reconstruction: The coefficient group is abelian; the two comparisons use distinct coefficient sheaves. Connectedness is retained for the announced Lie-group comparison. No general identification of Lie-algebra and classifying-space cohomology is inserted.
fate: The comparisons appear in \citet[Theorems 2 and 3]{geronimus1971lie}; the detailed classifying-space statement is \citet[Proposition 4.3]{geronimus1971topology}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Representation theory and the classification of particles
notes: Elementary-particle theory is incomplete because not all representations are known; spinors and electrons are mentioned.
statement: This motivates connecting particle descriptions with representation theory. No symmetry group, representation class, or mathematical completeness assertion is specified.
reconstruction: The remark is preserved without replacing it by a claim that physical theories are determined solely by a list of representations.
fate: The surrounding Geronimus construction supplies context \citep{geronimus1971topology}, but no precise mathematical claim or publication match follows.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is a research motivation, not a formulated mathematical problem.

title: The elliptic curve and the handwritten cubic exponent
notes: The scan reads \(y^3=x^3-g_1x-g_2\), with rational coefficients, and calls the curve elliptic.
statement: A smooth projective genus-one curve over \(\mathbb Q\) with a rational point is an elliptic curve. The written homogeneous cubic \(Y^3=X^3-g_1XZ^2-g_2Z^3\), if smooth, has the rational point \([1:1:0]\), so it can indeed define an elliptic curve. The familiar short Weierstrass equation instead has \(y^2\).
reconstruction: The exponent three is confirmed by the scan and is not automatically a mathematical error. Smoothness is missing; subsequent reduction is interpreted after passage to a minimal Weierstrass equation. No silent replacement of three by two is made.
fate: The Weierstrass-model conventions used for the subsequent arithmetic are in \citet[\S3.1]{cremona1997algorithms}. The intended equation is not determined beyond the surviving cubic.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: The congruence subgroup and compact modular curve
notes: \(\Gamma_0(A)\) consists of matrices \(\left(\begin{smallmatrix}\alpha&\beta\\A\gamma&\delta\end{smallmatrix}\right)\), but its displayed action is \((\alpha z+A\gamma)/(\beta z+\delta)\).
statement: For \(N\ge1\), \(\Gamma_0(N)=\{\left(\begin{smallmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{smallmatrix}\right)\in\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb Z):N\mid c\}\) acts on \(\mathfrak H\) by \(z\mapsto(az+b)/(cz+d)\). Adding cusps gives the compact modular curve \(X_0(N)\).
reconstruction: The off-diagonal entries are interchanged in the notebook action. The transposed subgroup is conjugate, but the written matrix and action cannot both be kept under the standard convention. A fundamental region is not yet the compact curve.
fate: The conventions are in \citet[\S\S2.1.1 and 2.15.1]{cremona1997algorithms}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Modularity of every elliptic curve over the rationals
notes: The Weil conjecture asserts a nontrivial analytic map \(X_A\to T\), with level \(A\) chosen as the conductor.
statement: For every elliptic curve \(E/\mathbb Q\) of conductor \(N\), there is a normalized weight-two cuspidal newform on \(\Gamma_0(N)\) with \(L(E,s)=L(f,s)\). Equivalently, \(E\) admits a nonconstant modular parametrization \(X_0(N)\to E\) over \(\mathbb Q\).
reconstruction: Nonconstant, compactification at cusps, and the arithmetic field are explicit. This is elliptic-curve modularity, not the Weil conjectures for varieties over finite fields.
fate: \citet[Theorem A and Introduction]{breuilconraddiamondtaylor2001modularity} proves modularity for all \(E/\mathbb Q\), completing the earlier semistable case. The integral parametrization is explained in \citet[\S\S2.6 and 2.15.1]{cremona1997algorithms}.
present_status: As of November 2026, solved by the modularity theorem; the full result was published in 2001.

title: There are not finitely many unrestricted maps to a torus
notes: A parenthesis says there are finitely many maps from every curve to a torus.
statement: Without normalization this is false: translating a map by arbitrary target points gives infinitely many maps, even constant ones. If a nonconstant \(\varphi:C\to E\) exists, the maps \([m]\circ\varphi\), \(m\ge1\), remain distinct after fixing a base point sent to zero, since their degrees grow as \(m^2\deg\varphi\).
reconstruction: The intended restriction, perhaps fixed degree or a quotient by operations on the target, is unspecified. These counterexamples do not require identifying that intention.
fate: The modular-parametrization construction \citep[\S2.15.1]{cremona1997algorithms} supplies examples of maps but does not support the unrestricted finiteness sentence.
present_status: As of November 2026, the literal assertion is false; an intended historical finiteness theorem cannot be uniquely recovered.

title: Reduction types and conductor exponents
notes: For \(p\ne2,3\), smooth reduction contributes \(A_p=1\), distinct tangents give \(A_p=p\), and coincident tangents give \(A_p=p^2\); \(A=\prod A_p\).
statement: For a minimal integral Weierstrass model over \(\mathbb Q_p\), good, multiplicative, and additive reduction have conductor exponents \(0,1,2\), respectively, for \(p\ge5\). Multiplicative reduction is split or nonsplit according to whether its tangent directions are defined over \(\mathbb F_p\). At \(p=2,3\), wild ramification can increase the additive exponent.
reconstruction: Minimality is essential. The global conductor includes exceptional primes, whose exponents the simple table does not determine. Split/nonsplit replaces real/imaginary over finite fields.
fate: Reduction and conductor computations are in \citet[\S\S3.1--3.2]{cremona1997algorithms}, including Tate\textquoteright s algorithm at exceptional primes. This modern source documents prior background, not a work claimed to precede the talk.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Local Euler factors of the elliptic-curve L-function
notes: At good primes \(L_p(s)=(1-c_pp^{-s}+p^{1-2s})^{-1}\), with \(\#E(\mathbb F_p)=1-c_p+p\); multiplicative reduction gives signs \(\pm1\), and additive reduction the factor one.
statement: At a good prime set \(a_p=p+1-\#E(\mathbb F_p)\), so \(L_p(E,s)=(1-a_pp^{-s}+p^{1-2s})^{-1}\). Split and nonsplit multiplicative primes give \((1-p^{-s})^{-1}\) and \((1+p^{-s})^{-1}\); additive primes give one. Their product defines \(L(E,s)\) in its initial half-plane of absolute convergence.
reconstruction: The factors use a minimal model and the correct reduction type. This elliptic \(L\)-function is not the full zeta function of a curve.
fate: The local data and matching coefficients are in \citet[\S\S2.6 and 3.9]{cremona1997algorithms}; equality with the modular \(L\)-series follows from \citet{breuilconraddiamondtaylor2001modularity}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: From Dirichlet coefficients to a weight-two modular form
notes: Expand \(\zeta(s)=\sum c_n/n_s\), then write \(\omega(z)=\sum c_ne^{inz}\).
statement: Write \(L(E,s)=\sum_{n\ge1}a_nn^{-s}\). Modularity states that \(f(z)=\sum_{n\ge1}a_ne^{2\pi inz}\) is the normalized weight-two newform of level \(N(E)\). Its invariant differential is \(2\pi i f(z)\,dz\).
reconstruction: The visible \(n_s\) is mathematically emended to \(n^s\). The factor \(2\pi\) uses the standard unit-period coordinate; \(e^{inz}\) requires rescaling coordinate and action. Forming the Fourier series does not prove modularity.
fate: The newform assertion is part of \citet[Introduction, Theorem A]{breuilconraddiamondtaylor2001modularity}; normalization is in \citet[\S2.6]{cremona1997algorithms}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Integrating the modular differential gives the parametrization
notes: \(\int\omega(z)\,dz\) is the sought map, and \(\int_z^{gz}\omega(z)\,dz\) should lie in a lattice for \(g\in\Gamma_0(A)\).
statement: The rational-coefficient newform attached to \(E\) has a rank-two period lattice \(\Lambda_f\). Integration from a base cusp defines \(X_0(N)\to\mathbb C/\Lambda_f\). This target is isogenous to \(E\); composition with an appropriate isogeny gives a parametrization of \(E\). Under \(\Gamma_0(N)\), the integral changes by a period.
reconstruction: The base point, invariant differential, quotient, and possible isogeny are supplied. The assertion does not hold for an arbitrary integer-coefficient Fourier series.
fate: \citet[\S2.15.1]{cremona1997algorithms} gives the period construction. Its applicability to every rational elliptic curve follows from \citet{breuilconraddiamondtaylor2001modularity}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: A positive compatible complex structure and a principal lattice
notes: \(B\) is nondegenerate skew and integral on \(L\); \(J^2=-1\), \(J^TBJ=B\), \(BJ>0\). The Hermitian form is \(H(z,w)=B(z,Jw)+iB(z,w)\).
statement: Let \((V,B)\) be real symplectic of dimension \(2N\), \(L\) a full integral lattice, and \(J\) a compatible complex structure with \(B(v,Jv)>0\) for nonzero \(v\). Then \(H\) is positive Hermitian, conjugate-linear in its first slot. Principality means \(B:L\to L^*\) is unimodular.
reconstruction: Volume one uses the symplectic normalization. Compatibility alone does not imply positivity; this is a separate condition, and nondegeneracy makes nonnegative positivity strict.
fate: These conventions are in \citet[\S\S1.1 and 1.2(c)]{cartier1968theta}; the notebook also refers to Cartier\textquoteright s earlier exposition \citep{cartier1966theta}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Quadratic refinements of the integral symplectic pairing
notes: \(F(\alpha+\beta)=F(\alpha)+F(\beta)+B(\alpha,\beta)\pmod2\); adding linear forms gives \(4^N\) solutions.
statement: Refinements of the alternating pairing on \(L/2L\) form an affine space over \(\operatorname{Hom}(L,\mathbb F_2)\). In a symplectic basis, \(F(m,n)=m\cdot n+\varepsilon\cdot m+\widetilde\varepsilon\cdot n\), with \(\varepsilon,\widetilde\varepsilon\in\mathbb F_2^N\); there are \(2^{2N}=4^N\) choices.
reconstruction: Only values modulo two matter; integer lifts give the same signs. The extra prime on one source coefficient does not affect the count.
fate: \citet[\S1.1]{cartier1968theta} develops this description.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Theta automorphy and its one-dimensional solution space
notes: Entire \(\Theta\) satisfies \(\Theta(z+\alpha)=(-1)^{F(\alpha)}e^{\pi H(\alpha,\alpha)/2+\pi H(\alpha,z)}\Theta(z)\), uniquely up to a constant for a principal lattice.
statement: For the positive compatible principally polarized data in 1970-228.1--2, the entire functions satisfying this law form a one-dimensional vector space. Nonzero solutions are unique up to nonzero scalar.
reconstruction: Positivity and principality are essential. Linearity of \(H\) in its second slot makes the factor holomorphic in \(z\); no conjugate of \(z\) should be inserted.
fate: The theta realization appears in \citet[\S1.3]{cartier1968theta} and is used in \citet[\S5]{perelomov1971completeness}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: The idempotent anecdote attributed to Pauli
notes: Gelfand writes \(P^2=P\), \(\lambda^2=\lambda\), then \(\lambda=0,+1,-1\), with \(-1\) discarded for physical reasons.
statement: Over \(\mathbb R\) or \(\mathbb C\), an eigenvalue of an idempotent satisfies \(\lambda(\lambda-1)=0\), hence is zero or one. Minus one is excluded algebraically.
reconstruction: This is an anecdote or joke, not silently changed into a different operator equation. No Pauli volume or passage is identified.
fate: No precise Pauli publication match was recovered from the book-and-idempotent wording. The correction follows directly from the written polynomial.
present_status: As of November 2026, the algebraic statement is settled; the anecdote	extquoteright s target is unidentified.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Coherent states, the Bargmann space, and its evaluation kernel
notes: \(a|\alpha\rangle=\alpha|\alpha\rangle\), labels fill \(\mathbb C\), and \(|\langle\alpha|\beta\rangle|^2=e^{-|\alpha-\beta|^2}\). Orthogonality means an entire function vanishes at the chosen labels.
statement: In \(\mathcal F^2=\{f\text{ entire}:\pi^{-1}\int_{\mathbb C}|f(z)|^2e^{-|z|^2}\,dA<\infty\}\), normalized kernels are \(k_\alpha(z)=e^{-|\alpha|^2/2+\bar\alpha z}\). With the inner product linear in the second slot, \(\langle k_\alpha,f\rangle=e^{-|\alpha|^2/2}f(\alpha)\). Their span is dense exactly when the labels form a uniqueness set. A finite accumulation point of distinct labels suffices by the identity theorem.
reconstruction: The conjugation convention and positive area measure are fixed. The Gaussian overlap kernel is positive definite, also by multiplying a Gram kernel entrywise with its conjugate; the marginal Neumann--Schoenberg reference supplies no distinct new theorem.
fate: The reduction and coherent-state formulas appear in \citet[\S\S1--2 and 4]{perelomov1971completeness}, published in February 1971.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: The critical area and the exact deletion threshold
notes: Cell area greater than \(\pi\) gives incompleteness, smaller area overcompleteness. At area \(\pi\), deleting one state leaves completeness, deleting two destroys it.
statement: For a full lattice \(\Lambda\subset\mathbb C\) with fundamental area \(S\), coherent states are incomplete for \(S>\pi\), and complete after every finite deletion for \(S<\pi\). At \(S=\pi\), the full system and every one-point deletion are complete, whereas every two-point deletion is incomplete.
reconstruction: The abbreviation means deleting points in context, not selecting only one or two. The critical excess-one statement is more precise than a density threshold.
fate: \citet[Assertion 1, \S4]{perelomov1971completeness} proves these exact alternatives. Received 20 August 1970, it appeared in February 1971; its 2002 arXiv date is a later archival posting.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Perelomov’s critical-lattice theta identity
notes: For \(\lambda_{mn}=m\omega_1+n\omega_2\) at area \(\pi\), \(\sum_{m,n}(-1)^{mn+m+n}e^{-|\lambda_{mn}|^2/2+\lambda_{mn}z}=0\); the notes call this one relation.
statement: If \(|\operatorname{Im}(\overline{\omega_1}\omega_2)|=\pi\), this series converges absolutely and uniformly on compact subsets of \(\mathbb C\) and vanishes identically. It is an identity of entire functions. Its coefficient signs are not square summable, so it is not automatically a norm-convergent dependence in the coherent-state Hilbert space.
reconstruction: Reflecting the lattice reconciles kernel conjugations. The informal one-relation statement concerns the completeness defect, not the kernel of an unspecified bounded synthesis operator.
fate: This is \citet[Eq.~(39) and the following theta argument]{perelomov1971completeness}. Whether it follows from a particular Jacobi identity concerns the proof route, not an unresolved identity.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Can an orthonormal basis have a uniformly bounded uncertainty product?
notes: Von Neumann\textquoteright s question asks whether \(\delta_x\delta_p\) stays bounded after orthogonalizing the critical coherent lattice. The notes then ask the general question for an orthogonal system; Gelfand thinks a positive answer unlikely.
statement: For unit vectors \(e_j\in L^2(\mathbb R)\), use centered standard deviations of position and Fourier momentum. There exists an orthonormal basis with \(\sup_j\Delta_x(e_j)\Delta_p(e_j)<\infty\). There even exists one with both centered second moments uniformly bounded. For a regular single-window Gabor basis, simultaneous finite second moments are impossible.
reconstruction: The scan expressly asks about the product. General basis existence, a particular Gram--Schmidt ordering of coherent states, and preservation of a fixed Gabor lattice are different formulations.
fate: Meyer\textquoteright s Schwartz wavelets give bounded product \citep[\S2, Theorem 1]{meyer1987uncertainty}, lectured February 1986 and published 1987. Bourgain\textquoteright s November 1986 preprint, published 1988, gives separate bounds \citep[Theorem, preprint p.~3]{bourgain1988uncertainty}. The distinction from Balian--Low and higher-moment obstructions appears in \citet[Eq.~(1.1), Theorem 1.1, pp.~115--116]{grochenigmalinnikova2013localization}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the unrestricted basis question has a positive established answer. An unspecified orthogonalization algorithm is not settled by this existence theorem.

title: Odd theta characteristics give the higher-dimensional identities
notes: The count is \(2^{N-1}(2^N-1)\), but the closing paragraph says half the \(4^N\) choices vanish. A Gaussian theta series equals \(c\Theta\).
statement: For a principal lattice, odd refinements number \(2^{N-1}(2^N-1)\), and even ones \(2^{N-1}(2^N+1)\). The Gaussian Poincaré series \(\sum_{\alpha\in L}(-1)^{F(\alpha)}e^{-\pi H(\alpha,\alpha)/2+\pi H(\alpha,z)}\) has the theta automorphy and is a scalar multiple of its theta function. It is even in \(z\); for an odd characteristic the theta function is odd, forcing the scalar to vanish.
reconstruction: The word half is false even for \(N=1\). Parity proves the odd-characteristic identities but does not exclude extra vanishing of even theta constants on special higher-dimensional tori.
fate: The refinement and parity framework appears in \citet[\S\S1.1 and 1.3]{cartier1968theta}; the theta-series argument is used in \citet[\S5]{perelomov1971completeness}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Weyl operators and the central lattice cocycle
notes: Heisenberg matrices are followed by \(D=e^{i\varphi}e^{i(\alpha^*a-\alpha a^*)}\). The subgroup uses lattice \(\alpha+i\beta\) and central coordinate \(k\pi\).
statement: With \([a,a^\dagger]=1\), unitary displacement operators are \(D(\alpha)=\exp(\alpha a^\dagger-\bar\alpha a)\), up to replacing \(\alpha\) by \(-\alpha\). Multiplication carries the symplectic phase cocycle. A lattice lift must incorporate it, equivalently a quadratic refinement; restricting a raw triangular central entry to \(\pi\mathbb Z\) need not give a subgroup for an arbitrary plane lattice.
reconstruction: The extra inner \(i\) turns a skew-adjoint exponent into a self-adjoint one and does not give the claimed unitary operator. Triangular and symmetric group coordinates have different central cocycles.
fate: The displacement and cocycle formulas are in \citet[\S5, Eqs.~(60)--(71)]{perelomov1971completeness}; the lattice lift is described by \citet[\S1.2]{cartier1968theta}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: The lattice model is irreducible after fixing the central character
notes: Induction from the signs \((-1)^{mn+m+n}\) on a discrete subgroup is said to give an irreducible representation.
statement: For the Heisenberg group with circle center \(T\), let \(\Gamma\) be the compatible lift of a principal lattice, with \(T\cap\Gamma=\{1\}\). Inducing from \(T\Gamma\) by the character \(\chi(t\gamma)=t\) gives the irreducible lattice realization of the Schrödinger representation with \(U_t=tI\). Induction from the discrete subgroup alone, or replacement by an arbitrary nontrivial central character, does not have this stated multiplicity-one conclusion.
reconstruction: The full center and its tautological character are essential. Principality is relative to this central weight; it does not give multiplicity one for every character \(t\mapsto t^m\).
fate: The exact formulation is \citet[\S1.2(b), pp.~420--421]{cartier1968theta}; the notebook abbreviates the essential central-character condition.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: Completeness for an arbitrary sequence of coherent states
notes: \ru{Для каких послед.} \(\lambda_n\) \ru{полная система?} The proof asks whether a nonzero Fock function can vanish at all labels.
statement: For a locally finite set \(\Lambda\subset\mathbb C\), characterize when no nonzero \(f\in\mathcal F^2\) vanishes on \(\Lambda\). Equivalently, characterize completeness of its coherent kernels. This is uniqueness, not the stronger stable sampling property.
reconstruction: Distinct labels and local finiteness isolate the nontrivial question. Finite accumulation is covered by 1970-228.5; area alone suffices only in the lattice case.
fate: A verified partial criterion is \citet[Definition 1.1, Theorem 1.2 and Remark 1.3]{mitkovskiwick2013uniqueness}, circulated 3 June 2013. In normalization \(e^{-\pi|z|^2}\), a \(d\)-regular perturbation \(\gamma_{mn}\) of \((m+in)/d\), with \(|m+in-d\gamma_{mn}|\le\phi(|m+in|)\), \(|\gamma_{mn}-\gamma_{m^{\prime}n^{\prime}}|\ge c|(m-m^{\prime})+i(n-n^{\prime})|\) for some \(c>0\), \(\phi(t)/t\) nonincreasing and \(\int_1^\infty\phi(t)t^{-2}dt<\infty\), is unique for \(d>1\), nonunique for \(d<1\); \(d=1\) admits both. A September 2026 zero-set preprint is an unverified lead \citep{houma2026zeros}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the lattice and stated perturbative cases are verified. Those results leave arbitrary irregular sets untreated; this audit has not established whether a complete modern characterization is available. The 2026 lead could not be opened, so no global claim of continued openness or resolution is made.
worth: A precise critical-density extension could merit work, but further development should first check the inaccessible 2026 lead and other recent classification results; no Stage 2 novelty claim is warranted here.

title: A proposed group-orbit generalization
notes: An intervention provisionally attributed to Kazhdan starts with \(T:G\to U(H)\), \(h_0\in H\), and discrete \(\Gamma\subset G\). For a reasonable subgroup, \(\{T(\gamma)h_0\}\) should be complete with finitely many relations.
statement: No group or representation class, cyclicity assumption, meaning of reasonable, or permitted topology and coefficients for relations is given. Completeness already fails if \(h_0\) lies in a proper invariant subspace.
reconstruction: The abbreviation after \(G\) is not expanded into a theorem about all semisimple groups. The coherent-state prototype does not determine the missing quantifiers.
fate: The Heisenberg model \citep[\S1.2]{cartier1968theta} and exact coherent-lattice result \citep{perelomov1971completeness} identify the prototype. No exact general-group theorem follows from this intervention.
present_status: As of November 2026, the generalization is too underspecified for a definite problem-index entry; no unsolved universal theorem is asserted.
speaker: D. A. Kazhdan (provisional attribution)

title: Finite-deletion overcompleteness
notes: Overcomplete means that throwing away any finite number of vectors leaves a complete system.
statement: A total family in a Hilbert space has the finite-deletion property if the complement of every finite subset still has dense linear span. This is stronger than some uses of overcomplete meaning merely redundant or nonminimal.
reconstruction: The notebook explicitly fixes its convention; no uniform frame bounds are implied.
fate: The lattice alternatives in \citet[Assertion 1]{perelomov1971completeness} distinguish this property from critical excess one.
present_status: As of November 2026, the reconstructed statement is established; no open problem is asserted.

title: The unnormalized complex-shift Gaussian series needs correction
notes: After the entire-function identity the notes write an alternative \(\sum_{m,n}(-1)^{mn+m+n}e^{-(x-\lambda_{mn})^2/2}\), with complex lattice labels.
statement: The literal complex-shift series need not even have terms tending to zero. For normalized oscillator coherent states write \(\alpha=(q+ip)/\sqrt2\) and \(\psi_\alpha(x)=\pi^{-1/4}\exp(-(x-q)^2/2+ip(x-q/2))\). The normalization and phase are essential when transporting a Bargmann identity to the position representation.
reconstruction: The second display is not justified by substituting complex centers into real normalized Gaussians. Its interpretation as a formal vector identity also needs the convergence qualifications in 1970-228.7.
